195	/// The process-wide place `CompositionBuilder` finds a document's reverse
196	/// resolution, keyed by the same `RecipeSource` slot the compositor reads
197	/// recipes under — `AudioDSPSource`'s shape, for `AudioDSPSource`'s reasons.
198	///
199	/// The two mirrors exist for the same underlying fact: `CompositionBuilder` is
200	/// handed the composition PLAN, and the plan is `plan.rs`'s structural
201	/// description of what to decode. `Source::Media.reversed` is deliberately not
202	/// in it — the core does no pixel work, so reversal changes neither the plan
203	/// nor the recipe (spec §11) — which leaves exactly one place for the answer
204	/// to arrive: beside the plan, published by the document.
205	///
206	/// **A key with no entry is answered by the handle, not by a search.** An
207	/// export mints a FRESH `RecipeSource` key so a queued frame cannot be
208	/// composed from a project the user changed mid-write, and nothing publishes
209	/// under that new key — but it does publish the project HANDLE under it, and a
210	/// handle is one object that exactly one document published. So the lookup
211	/// asks `RecipeSource` which handle the key was registered with and takes the
212	/// entry that published that same object.
213	///
214	/// It was once a scan for the document whose plan JSON matched. Reversal is
215	/// deliberately absent from the plan, so a reversed clip and a forward one
216	/// produce the SAME plan string: two such documents open at once were
217	/// indistinguishable to the scan, and the ambiguous answer — slate everything
218	/// either candidate called reversed — left a correctly rendered reversed clip
219	/// showing the missing-media plate in the preview and in the export, with no
220	/// way back. Measured, not theorised. Identity cannot be ambiguous, so the
221	/// case is gone rather than handled.
222	///
223	/// A key whose handle nobody published is still `.none`: no document claims
224	/// that composition, so no clip in it reads from a reversed file.
225	///
226	/// **And that handle search is only enough while the document has not moved
227	/// on, which is what a PIN is for.** The search names a document by the
228	/// object it published, and a document publishes a NEW object after every
229	/// edit, undo and live drag — `ProjectDocument.projectDidChange` calls
230	/// `publishReverseResolution`, which overwrites the document's one entry with
231	/// the current handle — and drops the entry outright when it closes. An
232	/// export that started a moment ago and finishes a moment later is never
233	/// caught by that; a QUEUED export, whose whole contract is that the person
234	/// goes back to editing while it waits, is caught by it every time. The
235	/// answer was `.none`, and `.none` is the one state this file's `ReverseStatus`
236	/// says cannot exist: `CompositionBuilder.fill` finds the clip in neither
237	/// `ready` nor `pending`, inserts the FORWARD asset track, and — because the
238	/// plan's `source_in` is measured in the REVERSED stream (`Source::Media` in
239	/// `core/src/model.rs`) — reads the mirrored window of the forward file, so a
240	/// trimmed clip shows different frames entirely. Unslated, unreported, in the
241	/// picture and in the sound alike, and measured by the loudness pass too.
242	///
243	/// So a caller that has captured a resolution and must keep it across an
244	/// edit PINS it to the handle it belongs to, and the pin is consulted only
245	/// AFTER the handle search fails. The order is deliberate: while the document
246	/// still holds that very handle, its own entry is the more current truth
247	/// about the disk — a reverse render that finished in the meantime republishes
248	/// under the SAME handle — so the pin answers exactly when the document has
249	/// moved on or gone, and nothing that worked before it existed behaves
250	/// differently. `ExportQueueController` is its one caller today; see
251	/// `pin(_:for:)` for what a caller owes.
252	final class ReverseSource {
253	    static let shared = ReverseSource()
254	
255	    private struct Entry {
256	        /// The handle this resolution was computed from. Compared, never
257	        /// dereferenced — it is here to name a document, and holding it
258	        /// strongly would keep a closed document's Rust project alive.
259	        let project: ObjectIdentifier
260	        let resolution: ReverseResolution
261	    }
262	
263	    /// A resolution held against one handle for the length of one write.
264	    ///
265	    /// Unlike `Entry` this RETAINS its project, and the difference is the
266	    /// point rather than an oversight: an `Entry` names a document that may
267	    /// close, where a pin names the handle a job is writing from right now.
268	    /// Holding it makes "a pin can never name a dead object" true here
269	    /// instead of true only while the caller happens to be retaining it too,
270	    /// and so closes the one way a pin could go wrong — an identity reused by
271	    /// a later allocation, answering some other project's frames.
272	    private struct Pin {
273	        let project: ReelProject
274	        let resolution: ReverseResolution
275	    }
276	
277	    private let lock = NSLock()
278	    private var entries: [Int: Entry] = [:]
279	    private var pins: [ObjectIdentifier: Pin] = [:]
280	
281	    private init() {}
282	
283	    /// Publishes a document's resolution. Main thread, after every edit and
284	    /// after every render that finishes.
285	    func publish(_ resolution: ReverseResolution, project: ReelProject, for key: Int) {
286	        lock.lock()
287	        defer { lock.unlock() }
288	        entries[key] = Entry(project: ObjectIdentifier(project), resolution: resolution)
289	    }
290	
291	    /// Drops a document's slot, the way `RecipeSource.unregister` does.
292	    func unpublish(_ key: Int) {
293	        lock.lock()
294	        defer { lock.unlock() }
295	        entries.removeValue(forKey: key)
296	    }
297	
298	    /// The resolution published for one HANDLE, whatever key it was published
299	    /// under — what a caller reads when it wants to keep the answer.
300	    ///
301	    /// Deliberately blind to the pins: this is the CAPTURE, and it must see
302	    /// the document's own current answer rather than something an earlier
303	    /// capture pinned.
304	    func resolution(publishedFor project: ReelProject) -> ReverseResolution {
305	        let handle = ObjectIdentifier(project)
306	        lock.lock()
307	        defer { lock.unlock() }
308	        return entries.values.first { $0.project == handle }?.resolution ?? .none
309	    }
310	
311	    /// Holds `resolution` against `project` until `unpin`, so a composition
312	    /// built from that handle still finds it after the document has edited,
313	    /// undone or closed its way onto a different one.
314	    ///
315	    /// **What the caller owes: exactly one `unpin` per `pin`, and a pin per
316	    /// handle at a time.** The table is keyed by identity, so a second pin of
317	    /// one handle replaces the first rather than stacking — the queue holds
318	    /// at most one because it runs one job at a time, which is where that
319	    /// invariant is stated and kept. A pin never released retains the Rust
320	    /// project behind the handle for the life of the process.
321	    func pin(_ resolution: ReverseResolution, for project: ReelProject) {
322	        lock.lock()
323	        defer { lock.unlock() }
324	        pins[ObjectIdentifier(project)] = Pin(project: project, resolution: resolution)
325	    }
326	
327	    /// Releases what `pin` held. Safe to call twice and safe to call for a
328	    /// handle that was never pinned.
329	    func unpin(_ project: ReelProject) {
330	        lock.lock()
331	        defer { lock.unlock() }
332	        pins.removeValue(forKey: ObjectIdentifier(project))
333	    }
334	
335	    /// What is pinned against `project`, or nil. Nothing in the app reads
336	    /// this — the resolution lookup below consults the table directly — and
337	    /// it is here so that a proof can assert the two halves a rendered frame
338	    /// cannot show: that a running job HAS pinned its captured answer, and
339	    /// that an idle queue has released every one of them.
340	    func pinnedResolution(for project: ReelProject) -> ReverseResolution? {
341	        lock.lock()
342	        defer { lock.unlock() }
343	        return pins[ObjectIdentifier(project)]?.resolution
344	    }
345	
346	    /// The resolution for the composition being built under `key`: the entry
347	    /// published under that key, the one published for the very handle the key
348	    /// was registered with, or — when the document has moved on from that
349	    /// handle — whatever a caller pinned to it. See the type's own comment for
350	    /// why the pin comes last.
351	    func resolution(for key: Int) -> ReverseResolution {
352	        lock.lock()
353	        let own = entries[key]
354	        lock.unlock()
355	        if let own = own { return own.resolution }
356	        guard let project = RecipeSource.shared.project(for: key) else { return .none }
357	        let handle = ObjectIdentifier(project)
358	        lock.lock()
359	        defer { lock.unlock() }
360	        if let published = entries.values.first(where: { $0.project == handle }) {
361	            return published.resolution
362	        }
363	        return pins[handle]?.resolution ?? .none
364	    }
365	}

372	/// Decodes one media file and writes it back to front, so AVFoundation can
373	/// play a reversed clip forward (spec §11: "reverse is not native; M3
374	/// pre-renders reversed segments").
375	///
376	/// **The reader-to-writer shape is `ExporterWriter`'s**, and deliberately so:
377	/// an `AVAssetReader` feeding an `AVAssetWriter`, cancelled by a flag every
378	/// sample checks, progress kept by hand because `AVAssetWriter` has none. What
379	/// differs is the ONE thing reversal forces — a writer's inputs take samples
380	/// in ascending presentation order, and the frames arrive in the opposite one,
381	/// so the file cannot be streamed through. Frames have to be held.
382	///
383	/// **Chunks, because holding the whole film is not an option.** The asset is
384	/// walked backwards a slice at a time: read `[t, t + Δ)` into memory, append
385	/// its frames newest-first, then step back to `[t − Δ, t)`. Δ is sized by
386	/// BYTES rather than by seconds — 4K frames are sixteen times a 720p frame —
387	/// so the resident cost is bounded whatever the source is, at the price of one
388	/// `AVAssetReader` per slice.
389	///
390	/// **The arithmetic that makes the reversed file line up with the model.**
391	/// The pivot is the media's own duration `T` as the model recorded it and the
392	/// subtraction is `ReverseMirror`'s, which states the convention and why the
393	/// app owns it; the reversal works only because it is exactly as long as the
394	/// original. Frame durations come out of the gaps between presentation stamps
395	/// rather than out of a nominal rate, which keeps a variable-rate source exact
396	/// instead of nearly right, and the written stream tiles `[0, T)` with no seam.
397	///
398	/// **What it does NOT do.**
399	/// * It does not carry the source's `preferredTransform`, and must not. A
400	///   custom compositor gets RAW decoded frames and turns the sampling itself
401	///   from the orientation code `CompositionBuilder.orientationCodes` reads off
402	///   the FORWARD asset (§7.5). The frames written here are the same coded
403	///   frames the forward file decodes to, so that one code is right for both;
404	///   baking a transform in would turn a portrait clip twice.
405	/// * It does not preserve an alpha channel. The intermediate (spec §11 PR-7)
406	///   is 10-bit 4:2:0 HEVC Main 10, or 10-bit 4:2:2 ProRes 422 when the source
407	///   has an odd width or height, so a reversed ProRes 4444 clip loses its
408	///   transparency — the price of an intermediate small enough to live in the
409	///   package, and not silent: the picture changes visibly when the clip is
410	///   reversed.
411	/// * It does not convert colour. The frames are read in the source's own
412	///   YCbCr at 10 bits, the held copy keeps the decoder's colour attachments,
413	///   and the encoder is given no colour properties, so the file carries the
414	///   source's own primaries, transfer and matrix — an HLG clip's reverse is
415	///   labelled HLG — and the compositor treats it exactly as it treats the
416	///   forward file (GR-15: HDR is converted there, at step 0, not here).
417	final class ReverseRenderer {
418	
419	    /// What one reverse is written as (spec §11 PR-7), from the source's
420	    /// coded size. HEVC 4:2:0 cannot hold an odd size — 1919×1079 came back
421	    /// 1918×1078 — and `videoSettings` says why the size must be exact, so an
422	    /// odd width or height takes ProRes 422, whose file is several times
423	    /// larger, for its exact size.
424	    enum Intermediate: Equatable {
425	        /// Even width and height: `x420` frames, HEVC Main 10.
426	        case hevcMain10
427	        /// An odd width or height: `x422` frames, ProRes 422 — full-range
428	        /// frames when the source is flagged full range (PR-10).
429	        case proRes422
430	
431	        init(_ dimensions: CMVideoDimensions) {
432	            self = dimensions.width % 2 != 0 || dimensions.height % 2 != 0 ? .proRes422 : .hevcMain10
433	        }
434	
435	        /// The format the reader is asked for, held, and handed the writer.
436	        var pixelFormat: OSType {
437	            switch self {
438	            case .hevcMain10: return REDACTED
439	            case .proRes422: return REDACTED
440	            }
441	        }
442	
443	        /// The format for a source whose forward video track is flagged
444	        /// `fullRange` (GR-22's flag, spec §11 PR-10): ProRes 422 reads
445	        /// full-range `x422`, because a full-range file read as video-range
446	        /// `x422` came back up to 90 codes off (log_proof L13, #289). The HEVC
447	        /// branch reads `pixelFormat` whatever the flag.
448	        func pixelFormat(fullRange: Bool) -> OSType {
449	            if fullRange && self == .proRes422 {
450	                return REDACTED
451	            }
452	            return pixelFormat
453	        }
454	
455	        /// Bytes one held pixel costs: 10-bit samples in 16-bit words, one
456	        /// luma and half (4:2:0) or one (4:2:2) chroma sample a pixel.
457	        var bytesPerPixel: Int {
458	            switch self {
459	            case .hevcMain10: return 3
460	            case .proRes422: return 4
461	            }
462	        }
463	    }
464	
465	    /// One media file to reverse, decided on the main thread against the
466	    /// document's snapshot so the render loop consults nothing that can move.
467	    struct Job: Equatable {
468	        let media: UInt32
469	        /// The media's display name, for the sheet's status line.
470	        let name: String
471	        let source: URL
472	        let destination: URL
473	        /// The media's duration as the MODEL has it — the pivot the reversal
474	        /// is measured about, and the number `in` is measured against.
475	        let duration: Ticks
476	        let fps: Fps
477	        let hasAudio: Bool
478	    }
479	
480	    enum ReverseError: LocalizedError {
481	        /// Nothing in the file can be reversed: no readable track, or a
482	        /// duration the model does not believe in.
483	        case unreadable(String)
484	        case cancelled
485	        case failed(String)
486	
487	        var errorDescription: String? {
488	            switch self {
489	            case .unreadable(let name):
490	                return "“\(name)” has no video or audio that can be reversed."
491	            case .cancelled:
492	                return "The reverse was cancelled."
493	            case .failed(let reason):
494	                return "The reversed clip could not be rendered: \(reason)"
495	            }
496	        }
497	    }
498	
499	    /// `MediaConsolidator.CancelToken`'s shape: one flag, one lock, safe from
500	    /// any thread and safe to set twice.
501	    final class CancelToken {
502	        private let lock = NSLock()
503	        private var flag = false
504	
505	        var isCancelled: Bool {
506	import AVFoundation
507	import VideoToolbox
508	
509	extension ReverseRenderer {
510	    // MARK: - Settings
511	
512	    /// The coded frame size, read from one decoded frame at the head of the
513	    /// file. Nil means "no picture", which an audio-only source really has and
514	    /// an unreadable video track amounts to.
515	    static func dimensions(
516	        of asset: AVURLAsset, track: AVAssetTrack, limit: CMTime
517	    ) -> CMVideoDimensions? {
518	        guard let reader = try? AVAssetReader(asset: asset) else { return nil }
519	        reader.timeRange = CMTimeRange(
520	            start: .zero,
521	            duration: CMTimeMinimum(limit, CompositionBuilder.time(ReelTime.perSecond)))
522	        let output = AVAssetReaderTrackOutput(
523	            track: track,
524	            outputSettings: [
525	                kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: Int(REDACTED)
526	            ])
527	        guard reader.canAdd(output) else { return nil }
528	        reader.add(output)
529	        guard reader.startReading() else { return nil }
530	        defer { reader.cancelReading() }
531	        guard let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer(),
532	            let format = CMSampleBufferGetFormatDescription(sample)
533	        else { return nil }
534	        return CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetDimensions(format)
535	    }
536	
537	    /// The encoder settings for the picture.
538	    ///
539	    /// **The size is the source's, exactly.** Not rounded to even, not scaled:
540	    /// the compositor maps the model's `source_size` across whatever texture
541	    /// arrives, so a reversed asset that is one pixel narrower than the
542	    /// forward one would stretch the clip the moment it is reversed.
543	    ///
544	    /// **10 bits at every size (spec §11 PR-7).** HEVC pinned to Main 10 —
545	    /// `ExporterWriter`'s `hevc_10bit` pin — fed the `x420` frames the reader
546	    /// decoded, at HEVC's rate: generous because this is an intermediate, its
547	    /// pixels encoded again on the way to the export, where a stingy one is a
548	    /// generation of loss the user did not ask for. An odd size is ProRes 422
549	    /// (`Intermediate`), which takes no compression dictionary.
550	    ///
551	    /// **No colour properties.** Given none, the writer labels the file by the
552	    /// frames' own attachments, which `copyBuffer` carries, so an HLG or a
553	    /// BT.2020 source is labelled as itself. Forcing BT.709 here mislabelled
554	    /// those sources, and with the attachments kept it would convert them.
555	    static func videoSettings(
556	        _ dimensions: CMVideoDimensions, fps: Fps, intermediate: Intermediate
557	    ) -> [String: Any] {
558	        let width = Int(dimensions.width)
559	        let height = Int(dimensions.height)
560	        guard intermediate == .hevcMain10 else {
561	            return [
562	                AVVideoCodecKey: AVVideoCodecType.proRes422,
563	                AVVideoWidthKey: width,
564	                AVVideoHeightKey: height,
565	            ]
566	        }
567	        let rate = fps.double > 0 ? fps.double : 30
568	        let bits = Int(
569	            min(max(Double(max(1, width * height)) * rate * 0.12, 2_000_000), 240_000_000))
570	        let compression: [String: Any] = [
571	            AVVideoAverageBitRateKey: bits,
572	            // A keyframe at least every two seconds, for the same reason the
573	            // export sets one: this file is scrubbed and seeked into on every
574	            // preview frame.
575	            AVVideoMaxKeyFrameIntervalDurationKey: 2.0,
576	            AVVideoExpectedSourceFrameRateKey: Int(rate.rounded()),
577	            AVVideoProfileLevelKey: kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel as String,
578	        ]
579	        return [
580	            AVVideoCodecKey: AVVideoCodecType.hevc,
581	            AVVideoWidthKey: width,
582	            AVVideoHeightKey: height,
583	            AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey: compression,
584	        ]
585	    }
586	
587	    /// How much of the source one slice covers: as many frames as the budget
588	    /// holds at the held format's bytes a pixel (`Intermediate`), turned back
589	    /// into time. An audio-only file has no frames to hold, so it takes long
590	    /// slices and pays for very few readers.
591	    static func sliceDuration(dimensions: CMVideoDimensions?, fps: Fps) -> CMTime {
592	        let rate = fps.double > 0 ? fps.double : 30
593	        guard let dimensions = dimensions, dimensions.width > 0, dimensions.height > 0 else {
594	            return CompositionBuilder.time(ReelTime.perSecond * 30)
595	        }
596	        let bytes =
597	            Int(dimensions.width) * Int(dimensions.height)
598	            * Intermediate(dimensions).bytesPerPixel
599	        let frames = min(max(bufferBudget / max(1, bytes), 4), 300)
600	        let ticks = Ticks((Double(frames) / rate * Double(ReelTime.perSecond)).rounded())
601	        return CompositionBuilder.time(max(ticks, 1))
602	    }
603	}

2	import AppKit
3	import VideoToolbox

5	// MARK: - Where a reversed asset lives
6	
7	/// The `cache/reversed/` half of the package (spec §5.6), and what makes one
8	/// of its files stale.
9	///
10	/// **Why inside the package.** §5.6 reserves `cache/` for data that is
11	/// regenerable and never required to open, and a reversed asset is exactly
12	/// that: delete it and the renderer makes it again from media the project
13	/// still references. It is regenerable in the strict sense and *expensive* in
14	/// the practical one — a ten-minute 4K clip is minutes of decode and encode —
15	/// so it belongs somewhere that travels with the edit rather than somewhere
16	/// that has to be rebuilt on the machine the package lands on.
17	/// `fileWrapper(ofType:)` already carries `cache/` across every save through
18	/// the LAZY `FileWrapper` the filmstrips ride, and `NSFileWrapper` hard-links
19	/// a child it is writing back over its own original — so a save in place pays
20	/// for the reverse once. A Save As, or an autosave to a new draft location,
21	/// really does copy it; that is the cost of a package that travels whole.
22	///
23	/// **Why not Application Support, where `FFmpegRewrap` puts its conversions.**
24	/// §11's reasoning for that choice does not transfer. A rewrap is the only
25	/// *decodable* copy of footage the app can open, so losing it loses the media;
26	/// a reverse is a derived rendering of media that is still there, so losing it
27	/// costs time. And a rewrap is made during an import, when the document is
28	/// usually still untitled and has no package — while a reverse is asked for
29	/// mid-edit, on a project that has one. An untitled document falls back to
30	/// `ProjectDocument`'s temporary cache directory exactly as filmstrips do, and
31	/// the first save copies the render into the package with everything else.
32	///
33	/// **Why the name carries a digest.** The contract's `<media id>.mov` names
34	/// the file by a project-scoped id, and ids outlive the file behind them:
35	/// Relink… can point media 3 at a completely different movie, and a reversed
36	/// asset for the old one would then be silently wrong — forward frames from
37	/// the wrong film. The digest is `FFmpegRewrap`'s (path, size, modification
38	/// second), for its reasons: it makes the render both reusable and
39	/// self-invalidating, and reading gigabytes to decide whether to re-encode
40	/// gigabytes is the wrong trade. It also covers `rendererVersion`, so a
41	/// render the renderer would now write differently — the 8-bit H.264/HEVC
42	/// files before spec §11 PR-7 — lands under a new name and is never reused;
43	/// `prune` deletes the old sibling when the new one arrives.
44	enum ReverseCache {
45	    /// The subdirectory of `cache/` this feature owns.
46	    static let directoryName = "reversed"
47	
48	    /// What the renderer writes, as a number in the digest. Bump it whenever
49	    /// the written file changes, so every reverse already in a package is
50	    /// rendered again rather than played. 2: the 10-bit intermediate with
51	    /// the source's colour labels (spec §11 PR-7). 3: an odd-size reverse of
52	    /// full-range media read as full-range frames (spec §11 PR-10). 4: a VP9
53	    /// media's range read from its `vpcC` (spec §11 GR-23). 5: an MP3 read
54	    /// past the encoder delay Core Audio leaves in (spec §11 SY-42).
55	    static let rendererVersion = 5
56	
57	    static func directory(in cache: URL) -> URL {
58	        cache.appendingPathComponent(directoryName, isDirectory: true)
59	    }
60	
61	    /// Where `media`'s reversal of `source` goes. nil when the source cannot
62	    /// be measured, which is the same answer as "there is nothing to reverse".
63	    static func destination(media: UInt32, source: URL, in cache: URL) -> URL? {
64	        guard let digest = digest(of: source) else { return nil }
65	        return directory(in: cache).appendingPathComponent("\(media)-\(digest).mov")
66	    }
67	
68	    /// A finished reversal already on disk, if there is one.
69	    static func existing(media: UInt32, source: URL, in cache: URL) -> URL? {
70	        guard let url = destination(media: media, source: source, in: cache),
71	            FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path)
72	        else { return nil }
73	        return url
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Throws away the reversals of `media` that a fresh one has just made
77	    /// obsolete — the previous digest's file after a relink, and any partial
78	    /// left by a render that died.
79	    ///
80	    /// Refuses to delete anything that is not a sibling of `keep` inside a
81	    /// directory named `reversed`, and refuses to delete `keep` itself. This
82	    /// takes a URL and removes files, which is the shape of function a bug
83	    /// elsewhere turns into data loss, so the guard is not a formality
84	    /// (`FFmpegRewrap.discard` makes the same one).
85	    static func prune(media: UInt32, keeping keep: URL) {
86	        let directory = keep.deletingLastPathComponent()
87	        guard directory.lastPathComponent == directoryName,
88	            let names = try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(atPath: directory.path)
89	        else { return }
90	        let kept = keep.lastPathComponent
91	        for name in names where name != kept && name.hasPrefix("\(media)-") {
92	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: directory.appendingPathComponent(name))
93	        }
94	    }
95	
96	    /// FNV-1a over path, byte size, modification second and `rendererVersion`
97	    /// — `FFmpegRewrap`'s digest plus the version, spelled again here rather
98	    /// than shared because that one is private to its own naming scheme and
99	    /// this one keys a different directory. Not a content hash, for the
100	    /// reason that file gives.
101	    private static func digest(of source: URL) -> String? {
102	        let attributes = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: source.path)
103	        guard let size = (attributes?[.size] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value else { return nil }
104	        let modified = (attributes?[.modificationDate] as? Date)?.timeIntervalSince1970 ?? 0
105	        var hash: UInt64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325
106	        for byte in "\(source.path)|\(size)|\(Int64(modified.rounded()))|v\(rendererVersion)".utf8 {
107	            hash = (hash ^ UInt64(byte)) &* 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3
108	        }
109	        let hex = String(hash, radix: 16)
110	        return String(repeating: "0", count: max(0, 16 - hex.count)) + hex
111	    }
112	}

114	// MARK: - What the composition is told
115	
116	/// Which clips play from a reversed file, and which are still waiting for one.
117	///
118	/// Keyed by CLIP and not by media, because reversal is a property of the clip:
119	/// the same movie forward on one track and backwards on another — the
120	/// boomerang every editor has made — is one media entry, two clips, and only
121	/// one of them may read the reversed file.
122	struct ReverseResolution: Equatable {
123	    /// Clip id → the pre-rendered file its segments read from instead of the
124	    /// media's own.
125	    let ready: [UInt32: URL]
126	    /// Clips that are reversed and have NO file yet: the render has not run,
127	    /// was cancelled, or failed. `CompositionBuilder` holds their place with
128	    /// empty time and marks them missing, so they draw §5.6's slate.
129	    ///
130	    /// This is the whole point of publishing pending clips rather than simply
131	    /// omitting them. A reversed clip with no reversed asset used to play
132	    /// FORWARD — the picture silently disagreed with the model — and a slate
133	    /// is the honest answer: something is meant to be here and is not.
134	    let pending: Set<UInt32>
135	    /// The document's `cache/ramp-audio/` (spec §11 SR-12 (b)), published
136	    /// beside the plan with the rest: a ramp segment plays its render when
137	    /// the file `RampAudioCache` names is in it when the composition is
138	    /// built, and is silent otherwise. Nil with no cache folder.
139	    var rampAudio: URL? = nil
140	    /// The document's `cache/isolated/` (spec §11 AU-52): an isolated clip
141	    /// plays its render when the file `IsolationCache` names is in it when
142	    /// the composition is built, and dry otherwise. Nil with no cache folder.
143	    var isolated: URL? = nil
144	    /// The document's cache folder (`intendedCacheDirectory`), where the
145	    /// gate's and the de-esser's level is read from (spec §11 AU-41,
146	    /// AU-42). Nil with none published: every such level is pending.
147	    var cache: URL? = nil
148	    /// The document's `cache/voiced/` (spec §11 AU-144), `isolated`'s
149	    /// sibling: a voiced clip plays its render when the file `VoiceCache`
150	    /// names is in it when the composition is built.
151	    var voiced: URL? {
152	        isolated.map {
153	            VoiceCache.directory(in: $0.deletingLastPathComponent())
154	        }
155	    }
156	
157	    static let none = ReverseResolution(ready: [:], pending: [])
158	
159	    var isEmpty: Bool { ready.isEmpty && pending.isEmpty }
160	}
161	
162	/// What the Clip tab's Timing section says about one clip's reverse, and the
163	/// state machine behind the "Render Reverse" button.
164	///
165	/// There is no state that means "reversed and playing forwards", which is the
166	/// point: every state below either has the frames or says out loud that it
167	/// does not.
168	enum ReverseStatus: Equatable {
169	    /// Not reversed — or reversed media that needs no rendering, which a
170	    /// still picture is.
171	    case off
172	    /// Reversed, with the backwards copy on disk.
173	    case ready
174	    /// Reversed, and its frames are being made or about to be.
175	    case pending
176	    /// Reversed, and the render was cancelled or failed. Nothing will retry it
177	    /// on its own; the button does.
178	    case stopped
179	    /// Reversed, but the media itself is missing or has no length — the clip
180	    /// is already drawing a missing-media slate for a different reason.
181	    case unavailable
182	
183	    /// The row's own words.
184	    var summary: String {
185	        switch self {
186	        case .off: return "—"
187	        case .ready: return "Rendered"
188	        case .pending: return "Rendering…"
189	        case .stopped: return "Not rendered"
190	        case .unavailable: return "Media missing"
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	
195	/// The process-wide place `CompositionBuilder` finds a document's reverse
196	/// resolution, keyed by the same `RecipeSource` slot the compositor reads
197	/// recipes under — `AudioDSPSource`'s shape, for `AudioDSPSource`'s reasons.
198	///
199	/// The two mirrors exist for the same underlying fact: `CompositionBuilder` is
200	/// handed the composition PLAN, and the plan is `plan.rs`'s structural
201	/// description of what to decode. `Source::Media.reversed` is deliberately not
202	/// in it — the core does no pixel work, so reversal changes neither the plan
203	/// nor the recipe (spec §11) — which leaves exactly one place for the answer
204	/// to arrive: beside the plan, published by the document.
205	///
206	/// **A key with no entry is answered by the handle, not by a search.** An
207	/// export mints a FRESH `RecipeSource` key so a queued frame cannot be
208	/// composed from a project the user changed mid-write, and nothing publishes
209	/// under that new key — but it does publish the project HANDLE under it, and a
210	/// handle is one object that exactly one document published. So the lookup
211	/// asks `RecipeSource` which handle the key was registered with and takes the
212	/// entry that published that same object.
213	///
214	/// It was once a scan for the document whose plan JSON matched. Reversal is
215	/// deliberately absent from the plan, so a reversed clip and a forward one
216	/// produce the SAME plan string: two such documents open at once were
217	/// indistinguishable to the scan, and the ambiguous answer — slate everything
218	/// either candidate called reversed — left a correctly rendered reversed clip
219	/// showing the missing-media plate in the preview and in the export, with no
220	/// way back. Measured, not theorised. Identity cannot be ambiguous, so the
221	/// case is gone rather than handled.
222	///
223	/// A key whose handle nobody published is still `.none`: no document claims
224	/// that composition, so no clip in it reads from a reversed file.
225	///
226	/// **And that handle search is only enough while the document has not moved
227	/// on, which is what a PIN is for.** The search names a document by the
228	/// object it published, and a document publishes a NEW object after every
229	/// edit, undo and live drag — `ProjectDocument.projectDidChange` calls
230	/// `publishReverseResolution`, which overwrites the document's one entry with
231	/// the current handle — and drops the entry outright when it closes. An
232	/// export that started a moment ago and finishes a moment later is never
233	/// caught by that; a QUEUED export, whose whole contract is that the person
234	/// goes back to editing while it waits, is caught by it every time. The
235	/// answer was `.none`, and `.none` is the one state this file's `ReverseStatus`
236	/// says cannot exist: `CompositionBuilder.fill` finds the clip in neither
237	/// `ready` nor `pending`, inserts the FORWARD asset track, and — because the
238	/// plan's `source_in` is measured in the REVERSED stream (`Source::Media` in
239	/// `core/src/model.rs`) — reads the mirrored window of the forward file, so a
240	/// trimmed clip shows different frames entirely. Unslated, unreported, in the
241	/// picture and in the sound alike, and measured by the loudness pass too.
242	///
243	/// So a caller that has captured a resolution and must keep it across an
244	/// edit PINS it to the handle it belongs to, and the pin is consulted only
245	/// AFTER the handle search fails. The order is deliberate: while the document
246	/// still holds that very handle, its own entry is the more current truth
247	/// about the disk — a reverse render that finished in the meantime republishes
248	/// under the SAME handle — so the pin answers exactly when the document has
249	/// moved on or gone, and nothing that worked before it existed behaves
250	/// differently. `ExportQueueController` is its one caller today; see
251	/// `pin(_:for:)` for what a caller owes.
252	final class ReverseSource {
253	    static let shared = ReverseSource()
254	
255	    private struct Entry {
256	        /// The handle this resolution was computed from. Compared, never
257	        /// dereferenced — it is here to name a document, and holding it
258	        /// strongly would keep a closed document's Rust project alive.
259	        let project: ObjectIdentifier
260	        let resolution: ReverseResolution
261	    }
262	
263	    /// A resolution held against one handle for the length of one write.
264	    ///
265	    /// Unlike `Entry` this RETAINS its project, and the difference is the
266	    /// point rather than an oversight: an `Entry` names a document that may
267	    /// close, where a pin names the handle a job is writing from right now.
268	    /// Holding it makes "a pin can never name a dead object" true here
269	    /// instead of true only while the caller happens to be retaining it too,
270	    /// and so closes the one way a pin could go wrong — an identity reused by
271	    /// a later allocation, answering some other project's frames.
272	    private struct Pin {
273	        let project: ReelProject
274	        let resolution: ReverseResolution
275	    }
276	
277	    private let lock = NSLock()
278	    private var entries: [Int: Entry] = [:]
279	    private var pins: [ObjectIdentifier: Pin] = [:]
280	
281	    private init() {}
282	
283	    /// Publishes a document's resolution. Main thread, after every edit and
284	    /// after every render that finishes.
285	    func publish(_ resolution: ReverseResolution, project: ReelProject, for key: Int) {
286	        lock.lock()
287	        defer { lock.unlock() }
288	        entries[key] = Entry(project: ObjectIdentifier(project), resolution: resolution)

292	    func unpublish(_ key: Int) {

294	        defer { lock.unlock() }
295	        entries.removeValue(forKey: key)

299	    /// under — what a caller reads when it wants to keep the answer.
300	    ///

302	    /// the document's own current answer rather than something an earlier
303	    /// capture pinned.
304	    func resolution(publishedFor project: ReelProject) -> ReverseResolution {
305	        let handle = ObjectIdentifier(project)
306	        lock.lock()
307	        defer { lock.unlock() }

312	    /// built from that handle still finds it after the document has edited,
313	    /// undone or closed its way onto a different one.

317	    /// one handle replaces the first rather than stacking — the queue holds
318	    /// at most one because it runs one job at a time, which is where that
319	    /// invariant is stated and kept. A pin never released retains the Rust

321	    func pin(_ resolution: ReverseResolution, for project: ReelProject) {
322	        lock.lock()
323	        defer { lock.unlock() }

328	    /// handle that was never pinned.

331	        defer { lock.unlock() }

336	    /// this — the resolution lookup below consults the table directly — and

338	    /// cannot show: that a running job HAS pinned its captured answer, and
339	    /// that an idle queue has released every one of them.
340	    func pinnedResolution(for project: ReelProject) -> ReverseResolution? {
341	        lock.lock()
342	        defer { lock.unlock() }
343	        return pins[ObjectIdentifier(project)]?.resolution
344	    }

346	    /// The resolution for the composition being built under `key`: the entry
347	    /// published under that key, the one published for the very handle the key
348	    /// was registered with, or — when the document has moved on from that
349	    /// handle — whatever a caller pinned to it. See the type's own comment for
350	    /// why the pin comes last.
351	    func resolution(for key: Int) -> ReverseResolution {
352	        lock.lock()
353	        let own = entries[key]
354	        lock.unlock()

359	        defer { lock.unlock() }

361	            return published.resolution

372	/// Decodes one media file and writes it back to front, so AVFoundation can
373	/// play a reversed clip forward (spec §11: "reverse is not native; M3
374	/// pre-renders reversed segments").
375	///
376	/// **The reader-to-writer shape is `ExporterWriter`'s**, and deliberately so:
377	/// an `AVAssetReader` feeding an `AVAssetWriter`, cancelled by a flag every
378	/// sample checks, progress kept by hand because `AVAssetWriter` has none. What
379	/// differs is the ONE thing reversal forces — a writer's inputs take samples
380	/// in ascending presentation order, and the frames arrive in the opposite one,
381	/// so the file cannot be streamed through. Frames have to be held.
382	///
383	/// **Chunks, because holding the whole film is not an option.** The asset is
384	/// walked backwards a slice at a time: read `[t, t + Δ)` into memory, append
385	/// its frames newest-first, then step back to `[t − Δ, t)`. Δ is sized by
386	/// BYTES rather than by seconds — 4K frames are sixteen times a 720p frame —
387	/// so the resident cost is bounded whatever the source is, at the price of one
388	/// `AVAssetReader` per slice.
389	///
390	/// **The arithmetic that makes the reversed file line up with the model.**
391	/// The pivot is the media's own duration `T` as the model recorded it and the
392	/// subtraction is `ReverseMirror`'s, which states the convention and why the
393	/// app owns it; the reversal works only because it is exactly as long as the
394	/// original. Frame durations come out of the gaps between presentation stamps
395	/// rather than out of a nominal rate, which keeps a variable-rate source exact
396	/// instead of nearly right, and the written stream tiles `[0, T)` with no seam.
397	///
398	/// **What it does NOT do.**
399	/// * It does not carry the source's `preferredTransform`, and must not. A
400	///   custom compositor gets RAW decoded frames and turns the sampling itself
401	///   from the orientation code `CompositionBuilder.orientationCodes` reads off
402	///   the FORWARD asset (§7.5). The frames written here are the same coded
403	///   frames the forward file decodes to, so that one code is right for both;
404	///   baking a transform in would turn a portrait clip twice.
405	/// * It does not preserve an alpha channel. The intermediate (spec §11 PR-7)
406	///   is 10-bit 4:2:0 HEVC Main 10, or 10-bit 4:2:2 ProRes 422 when the source
407	///   has an odd width or height, so a reversed ProRes 4444 clip loses its
408	///   transparency — the price of an intermediate small enough to live in the
409	///   package, and not silent: the picture changes visibly when the clip is
410	///   reversed.
411	/// * It does not convert colour. The frames are read in the source's own
412	///   YCbCr at 10 bits, the held copy keeps the decoder's colour attachments,
413	///   and the encoder is given no colour properties, so the file carries the
414	///   source's own primaries, transfer and matrix — an HLG clip's reverse is
415	///   labelled HLG — and the compositor treats it exactly as it treats the
416	///   forward file (GR-15: HDR is converted there, at step 0, not here).
417	final class ReverseRenderer {
418	
419	    /// What one reverse is written as (spec §11 PR-7), from the source's
420	    /// coded size. HEVC 4:2:0 cannot hold an odd size — 1919×1079 came back
421	    /// 1918×1078 — and `videoSettings` says why the size must be exact, so an
422	    /// odd width or height takes ProRes 422, whose file is several times
423	    /// larger, for its exact size.
424	    enum Intermediate: Equatable {
425	        /// Even width and height: `x420` frames, HEVC Main 10.
426	        case hevcMain10
427	        /// An odd width or height: `x422` frames, ProRes 422 — full-range
428	        /// frames when the source is flagged full range (PR-10).
429	        case proRes422
430	
431	        init(_ dimensions: CMVideoDimensions) {
432	            self = dimensions.width % 2 != 0 || dimensions.height % 2 != 0 ? .proRes422 : .hevcMain10
433	        }
434	
435	        /// The format the reader is asked for, held, and handed the writer.
436	        var pixelFormat: OSType {
437	            switch self {
438	            case .hevcMain10: return REDACTED
439	            case .proRes422: return REDACTED
440	            }
441	        }
442	
443	        /// The format for a source whose forward video track is flagged
444	        /// `fullRange` (GR-22's flag, spec §11 PR-10): ProRes 422 reads
445	        /// full-range `x422`, because a full-range file read as video-range
446	        /// `x422` came back up to 90 codes off (log_proof L13, #289). The HEVC
447	        /// branch reads `pixelFormat` whatever the flag.
448	        func pixelFormat(fullRange: Bool) -> OSType {
449	            if fullRange && self == .proRes422 {
450	                return REDACTED
451	            }
452	            return pixelFormat
453	        }
454	
455	        /// Bytes one held pixel costs: 10-bit samples in 16-bit words, one
456	        /// luma and half (4:2:0) or one (4:2:2) chroma sample a pixel.
457	        var bytesPerPixel: Int {
458	            switch self {
459	            case .hevcMain10: return 3
460	            case .proRes422: return 4
461	            }
462	        }
463	    }
464	
465	    /// One media file to reverse, decided on the main thread against the
466	    /// document's snapshot so the render loop consults nothing that can move.
467	    struct Job: Equatable {
468	        let media: UInt32
469	        /// The media's display name, for the sheet's status line.
470	        let name: String
471	        let source: URL
472	        let destination: URL
473	        /// The media's duration as the MODEL has it — the pivot the reversal
474	        /// is measured about, and the number `in` is measured against.
475	        let duration: Ticks
476	        let fps: Fps
477	        let hasAudio: Bool
478	    }
479	
480	    enum ReverseError: LocalizedError {
481	        /// Nothing in the file can be reversed: no readable track, or a
482	        /// duration the model does not believe in.
483	        case unreadable(String)
484	        case cancelled
485	        case failed(String)
486	
487	        var errorDescription: String? {
488	            switch self {
489	            case .unreadable(let name):
490	                return "“\(name)” has no video or audio that can be reversed."
491	            case .cancelled:
492	                return "The reverse was cancelled."
493	            case .failed(let reason):
494	                return "The reversed clip could not be rendered: \(reason)"
495	            }
496	        }
497	    }
498

500	    /// any thread and safe to set twice.
501	    final class CancelToken {
502	        private let lock = NSLock()
503	        private var flag = false
504	
505	        var isCancelled: Bool {

507	import VideoToolbox

509	extension ReverseRenderer {
510	    // MARK: - Settings
511	
512	    /// The coded frame size, read from one decoded frame at the head of the
513	    /// file. Nil means "no picture", which an audio-only source really has and
514	    /// an unreadable video track amounts to.
515	    static func dimensions(
516	        of asset: AVURLAsset, track: AVAssetTrack, limit: CMTime
517	    ) -> CMVideoDimensions? {
518	        guard let reader = try? AVAssetReader(asset: asset) else { return nil }
519	        reader.timeRange = CMTimeRange(
520	            start: .zero,
521	            duration: CMTimeMinimum(limit, CompositionBuilder.time(ReelTime.perSecond)))
522	        let output = AVAssetReaderTrackOutput(
523	            track: track,
524	            outputSettings: [
525	                kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: Int(REDACTED)
526	            ])
527	        guard reader.canAdd(output) else { return nil }
528	        reader.add(output)
529	        guard reader.startReading() else { return nil }
530	        defer { reader.cancelReading() }
531	        guard let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer(),
532	            let format = CMSampleBufferGetFormatDescription(sample)
533	        else { return nil }
534	        return CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetDimensions(format)
535	    }
536	
537	    /// The encoder settings for the picture.
538	    ///
539	    /// **The size is the source's, exactly.** Not rounded to even, not scaled:
540	    /// the compositor maps the model's `source_size` across whatever texture
541	    /// arrives, so a reversed asset that is one pixel narrower than the
542	    /// forward one would stretch the clip the moment it is reversed.
543	    ///
544	    /// **10 bits at every size (spec §11 PR-7).** HEVC pinned to Main 10 —
545	    /// `ExporterWriter`'s `hevc_10bit` pin — fed the `x420` frames the reader
546	    /// decoded, at HEVC's rate: generous because this is an intermediate, its
547	    /// pixels encoded again on the way to the export, where a stingy one is a
548	    /// generation of loss the user did not ask for. An odd size is ProRes 422
549	    /// (`Intermediate`), which takes no compression dictionary.
550	    ///
551	    /// **No colour properties.** Given none, the writer labels the file by the
552	    /// frames' own attachments, which `copyBuffer` carries, so an HLG or a
553	    /// BT.2020 source is labelled as itself. Forcing BT.709 here mislabelled
554	    /// those sources, and with the attachments kept it would convert them.
555	    static func videoSettings(
556	        _ dimensions: CMVideoDimensions, fps: Fps, intermediate: Intermediate
557	    ) -> [String: Any] {
558	        let width = Int(dimensions.width)
559	        let height = Int(dimensions.height)
560	        guard intermediate == .hevcMain10 else {
561	            return [
562	                AVVideoCodecKey: AVVideoCodecType.proRes422,
563	                AVVideoWidthKey: width,
564	                AVVideoHeightKey: height,
565	            ]
566	        }
567	        let rate = fps.double > 0 ? fps.double : 30
568	        let bits = Int(
569	            min(max(Double(max(1, width * height)) * rate * 0.12, 2_000_000), 240_000_000))
570	        let compression: [String: Any] = [
571	            AVVideoAverageBitRateKey: bits,
572	            // A keyframe at least every two seconds, for the same reason the
573	            // export sets one: this file is scrubbed and seeked into on every
574	            // preview frame.
575	            AVVideoMaxKeyFrameIntervalDurationKey: 2.0,
576	            AVVideoExpectedSourceFrameRateKey: Int(rate.rounded()),
577	            AVVideoProfileLevelKey: kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel as String,
578	        ]
579	        return [
580	            AVVideoCodecKey: AVVideoCodecType.hevc,
581	            AVVideoWidthKey: width,
582	            AVVideoHeightKey: height,
583	            AVVideoCompressionPropertiesKey: compression,
584	        ]
585	    }
586	
587	    /// How much of the source one slice covers: as many frames as the budget
588	    /// holds at the held format's bytes a pixel (`Intermediate`), turned back
589	    /// into time. An audio-only file has no frames to hold, so it takes long
590	    /// slices and pays for very few readers.
591	    static func sliceDuration(dimensions: CMVideoDimensions?, fps: Fps) -> CMTime {
592	        let rate = fps.double > 0 ? fps.double : 30
593	        guard let dimensions = dimensions, dimensions.width > 0, dimensions.height > 0 else {
594	            return CompositionBuilder.time(ReelTime.perSecond * 30)
595	        }
596	        let bytes =
597	            Int(dimensions.width) * Int(dimensions.height)
598	            * Intermediate(dimensions).bytesPerPixel
599	        let frames = min(max(bufferBudget / max(1, bytes), 4), 300)
600	        let ticks = Ticks((Double(frames) / rate * Double(ReelTime.perSecond)).rounded())
601	        return CompositionBuilder.time(max(ticks, 1))
602	    }
603	}

content.content:
`rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `set_action_end` with a
`speed` and `remove_action` re-time captions as above, and their answer
carries `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` (caption clip ids), each
only when it is not empty.

## Reverse a clip

Reverse lives in the **Timing** section of the inspector's **Clip** tab, on the
**Clip** sub-tab. With one clip selected, Timing shows In, Out and Duration
above the Reverse rows. With several media clips selected, it shows only the
Reverse rows, and they apply to every selected media clip as one undo step.

| Row | What it shows or does |
|---|---|
| **Reverse** | A checkbox: play the clip back to front, picture and sound, or forwards again. Undo step: **Reverse**. |
| **Reversed frames** | The state of the backwards copy: `—` (not reversed), `Rendering…`, `Rendered`, `Not rendered` or `Media missing`. |
| **Render Reverse** | Starts the render again after it was cancelled or failed. Available only in the `Not rendered` state. |

Reversing never moves the clip: it keeps its start, its length and its in
point. The in point is counted in the direction the clip plays, so reversing
a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file.

Reverse works together with Speed, Fit to, the ⌥ rate stretch and speed
ramps. The in point and the ramp both count in the direction the clip plays,
so a reversed ramped clip ramps through the file backwards.

### The Reversing sheet

The system's playback cannot play video backwards, so Frame Job renders a
backwards copy of the file once. The copy is kept in the project package and
shared by every reversed clip of that file. When you tick Reverse on a file
with no copy yet, the **Reversing** sheet appears with a progress bar and the
line "Rendering a reversed copy of “name”…" (or "Rendering reversed copies of
N files…"). The status reads "Preparing…" until the render starts.

- When it finishes, the sheet closes and the clip plays backwards.
- **Cancel** stops the render; the sheet reads "Stopping…" until it has. It
  then reads "Stopped. Clips that are still reversed show a slate until their
  frames are rendered — press Render Reverse in the Timing section of the Clip
  tab to try again." and offers **Close**.
- If a file cannot be reversed, the sheet says how many files failed and
  names the first.

Until a clip's backwards copy exists, it shows a slate instead of playing
forwards. Nothing restarts a stopped render by itself: press **Render
Reverse**. Each press renders one file, shared by every reversed clip of
that file, so press it once for each file whose clips still show `Not
rendered`. A reversed copy of a 10-bit source keeps
its 10-bit depth and its colour labels.

A still image needs no rendering, since it looks the same backwards.

*Agents:* `set_reversed` (`clip`, `reversed` true or false; it is required,
not a toggle).

## Freeze frame

**Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** (⇧⌘F) holds the frame under the playhead for 2 s:

1. The clip is split at the playhead.
2. 2 s of empty time opens at the playhead across every unlocked track, so
   everything after it moves later together and stays in sync.
3. A still of that exact source frame fills the gap on the clip's track.

The still keeps the clip's look exactly as it was at that moment, including
position, scale, crop and any action that was moving it, so the held frame
lines up with the frame it froze. The still has no actions of its own. On a
ramped or speed-changed clip it holds the frame actually playing at the
playhead.

To hold a different frame, ⌥⇧-drag the still's body (a slip, undo step
**Slip**). The still stays where it is and holds an earlier or later frame
of the source.

The command works on a **selected** clip under the playhead and is available
only when there is one. It needs a clip with a picture: an audio-only clip,
text, a shape or another still cannot be frozen. If the still would break the
overlap rule, the freeze is refused and nothing changes. Undo step: **Freeze
Frame**.

*Agents:* `freeze_frame` (`clip`, optional `at`, which defaults to the
playhead, and `duration`, which defaults to 2 s). `slip` on a freeze clip
moves the frame it holds.

## Limits

- Speed, Fit to, rate stretch, speed ramps, reverse and freeze frame work on
  media clips only. Via an agent, any other kind of clip is an error, not a
  refusal.
- A rate is always between ×0.1 and ×1000. The Speed and Speed Ramp…
  sheets do not accept a value outside that range, the inspector clamps a
  typed value to it, and a rate stretch beyond it does nothing.
- Above ×12 a clip has no sound. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere
  silences the whole clip.
- A speed ramp never changes the clip's start or length, and an edit that
  would make it play past the end of its file is refused.

guide_errors: docs/guide/speed.md:438: 'The status reads "Preparing…" until the render starts.' The user never sees this. app/Sources/ReverseProgressSheetController.swift:29 sets "Preparing…" as the label's initial text, but loadView (:53-56) overwrites it before the sheet appears.

docs/guide/speed.md:455: 'A still image needs no rendering, since it looks the same backwards.' This describes a state no one can reach. A picture is an image clip with no Reverse rows (app/Sources/ClipPane+Timing.swift:95, core/src/edit_clip.rs:171), and set_reversed is an error on it (core/src/edit_clip.rs:415-424).

docs/guide/speed.md:479-481: Freeze Frame 'is available only when there is one' and 'needs a clip with a picture'. The menu item tests only for a selected clip under the playhead (app/Sources/EditorViewController+Timeline.swift:481-483). On any other clip it stays enabled and shows the error 'clip N is not a media clip' or 'clip N has no video properties' (core/src/edit_time.rs:505-513). The guide's list also leaves out picture, graphic, adjustment and nest clips.

docs/guide/speed.md:479-482: 'If the still would break the overlap rule, the freeze is refused' does not say where this happens: inside a transition and on a locked track, which always refuses (core/src/edit_time.rs:596, core/src/transition.rs:281-331).
data.notes:
Pages checked: docs/site/src/content/docs/speed/reverse.mdx and docs/site/src/content/docs/speed/freeze-frame.mdx. check-pages.mjs and docs_site_proof.py both report 0 problems after the edits. No heading changed, so the anchors file is untouched.

The claim count of 112 is approximate.

One problem is outside my pages: docs/site/src/content/docs/mcp/tools-speed.mdx:208 repeats the windowless claim I removed ("A project open with no window shows no sheet and starts no render, so its reversed clips stay on the slate until the project is opened in a window."). It should get the same fix from whoever owns that page.

Three claims have weaker evidence than the rest:
- "several times larger" for ProRes 422 rests on a code comment (app/Sources/ReverseRenderer.swift, Intermediate). The HEVC bitrate formula in app/Sources/ReverseRenderer+Settings.swift is consistent with it, so I kept the claim.
- "Two places do this" on freeze-frame was worked through from the rules. A locked track always refuses. Inside a transition refuses in the ordinary case, but when the overlapping clip ends within about 1 s of the playhead the still can fit, so it is not absolute. I kept it as written.
- The video half of a reversed ramp was not traced through the composition builder. The audio side is confirmed (app/Sources/RampAudioCache.swift reads the reversed file), and nothing in the core refuses the combination.

Nothing on either page depends on FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS or an -RCDev default now that the windowless sentence is gone.
